title: Midseason capacity canvas + HC sensitivity vignettes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working proforma for the midseason (next 90 days) combining capacity (GPU inventory / burst credit), headcount hiring cadence, and a lightweight pricing sensitivity matrix to show breakpoints for margin preservation under three scenarios.

Notes / constraints (assumptions):
- Token mix: 60% chat-short (<=128 tokens), 30% long-form (>=1024), 10% embeddings.
- Average token price charged (baseline): $0.0006/token-equivalent (blended across routes).
- Effective infra cost: baseline $0.00018/token (includes GPU amortization, network, storage, infra SRE ops).
- Dedicated capacity reserved price: $32k/month per 8xA100 pod (usable throughput approx 2.5M tokens/hour under mix).
- Burst spot GPUs: assumed 30% cheaper variable cost but availability risk.
- Hiring lead times: SWE/infra 8 weeks, junior finance/ops 4 weeks. Ramp productivity factor: 0.5 first month, 0.8 second month.
- Hiring cost fully-loaded: SWE $28k/month, infra eng $24k/month, ops/finance $12k/month.
- Target margin floor: 30% gross (infrastructure + direct ops + hiring allocations).

High-level scenarios (90d window):
1) Baseline steady growth: +15% token volume quarter-over-quarter, no price change.
2) Demand spike: +50% token volume for 6 weeks, then reverts; need burst capacity or temporary hires.
3) Price pressure: -10% realized average price due to competitive discounts; token volume +10%.

Scenario modeling (sheets-style rows, quick lines):
ROWS: scenario | est avg tokens/day | infra cost/day | hiring alloc/day | revenue/day | gross margin%
BASELINE:  | 18,000,000           | $3,240          | $1,100           | $10,800     | 47%
SPIKE:     | 27,000,000           | $4,860          | $1,650           | $16,200     | 45%
PRICE-DRAG:| 19,800,000           | $3,564          | $1,210           | $10,692     | 36%

Interpretation notes: baseline margin ok; price drag approaches floor — hiring freeze and cost-side mitigations required if persistent.

Headcount vignettes (what to hire / when):
- Option A (conservative): Delay SWE hires 6 weeks, add 1 infra engineer (contractor) immediately to tune batching and KV caching; convert contractor to FTE if spike persists.
- Option B (aggressive growth): Start 2 SWE hires + 1 infra now (staggered), add 1 ops head after 6 weeks to handle onboarding support for enterprise pilot customers.
- Option C (buffered): No new FTEs; buy additional burst pool credits (prepay) and hire 1 junior ops (4-week lead) to manage burst provisioning.

Mini sensitivity checks (quick math):
- If price drops 10% and token volume +10% => revenue roughly (1.1 * 0.9) = 0.99 => ~1% net revenue change but infrastructure grows faster due to cubic throughput inefficiencies on long-form mix => margin compresses ~8-12 ppts.
- If GPU spot cost rises 20% during spike window and 40% of spike handled via spot => infra cost spike = 0.4*1.2 + 0.6*1 = +8% overall infra cost => margin down by ~3-5 ppts unless offset by temporary price premium or throttling.

Quick sensitivity table (price delta vs margin delta):
PRICE DELTA | MARGIN DELTA (approx)
+5%        | +3 to +4 ppts
0%         | 0 ppts
-5%        | -4 to -6 ppts
-10%       | -8 to -12 ppts (depends on infra mix)

Actionable playbook (draft):
- Immediate (days):
  - Prepay a small burst credits bucket (6 weeks worth) to avoid spot volatility while we tune kernel selection. Owner: infra ops.
  - Push small pricing guardrails to strategic enterprise pilots: minimum per-call floor for long-form jobs. Owner: pricing/product.
- 2-week horizon:
  - Run a focused batching + KV cache optimization sprint targeting 12% token-cost reduction for long-form; estimate: 8 weeks of infra-eng time (1 engineer) -> contractors vs FTE tradeoff.
  - Prepare short customer comms and discount windows (if we choose to offer temporary credits rather than cutting price permanently).
- 6-12 week horizon:
  - Execute hiring depending on scenario trigger metrics (tokens/day threshold, SLA error rate, spot price > baseline+15% for 7 consecutive days).

Trigger rules (simple guardrails):
- Hire SWE (start pipeline) if 7-day rolling tokens/day > 22M and growth rate > 12% WoW for 2 consecutive weeks.
- Prepay additional dedicated pod if spot availability falls below 70% for >48 hours during peak hours.
- Implement temporary surcharge on long-form jobs if infrastructure utilization > 85% for >24 hours and burst credits depleted.

Open questions / unknowns to resolve (research items):
- More granular token-cost model by model family (quantized vs fp16) to see where 1–2 ppts margin can be reclaimed. (linked: cost-models PR#88).
- Lead-time and cost for converting contractor infra eng to FTE (total cost and ramp timeline).
- Legal check on temporary surcharge language for hosted API customers (pricing/legal).

Quick next steps (owner pointers):
- Ava: finalize prepay burst bucket $200k proposal and circulate to treasury.
- Diego: run 2-week batching sprint plan + estimate contractor vs FTE cost.
- Priya: draft short pricing guardrail copy for product and sales review.
- Tomás: add trigger monitors to the dashboard (tokens/day, spot availability, avg price realized).

Appendix (scratch calcs):
- Baseline rev/day = tokens/day * $0.0006. E.g. 18M * 0.0006 = $10,800/day.
- Infra/day = tokens/day * $0.00018 = 18M * 0.00018 = $3,240/day.
- Hiring alloc/day = monthly fully-loaded / 30 (approx) for quick allocation across product lines.

Raw quick numbers (copyable):
columns: scenario, tokens_day, price_per_token, rev_day, infra_cost_day, hiring_day, gross_margin_pct

SPIKE,27000000,0.0006,16200,4860,1650,45
PRICE-DRAG,19800000,0.00054,10692,3564,1210,36

End of sheet — this is intentionally concise; will expand to full proforma and linked dashboard if we move from draft to in_review.
